sources.locator: "Soviet invasion of Manchuria", revision 1376133899, lead: "often considered a major factor, alongside the atomic bombings, in the Japanese government’s decision to surrender"

explanation: “Soviet invasion of Manchuria”, at revision 1376133899, lead: “The Soviet entry into the war against Japan and the defeat of the Kwantung Army are often considered a major factor, alongside the atomic bombings, in the Japanese government’s decision to surrender unconditionally by 15 August.” That is a cause stated and hedged, so `probable` and not `consensus`: the article says the link is widely held, not settled, and A2 allows `consensus` only through a work Wikipedia cites. The companion edge `atomic-bombings-of-hiroshima-and-nagasaki--surrender-of-japan--caused` is `disputed` and names this event in its own `dispute.text` as the competing cause; with this record the atlas holds both sides of that argument and a reader can walk it. The same article’s § Aftermath states the link again — “The invasion of Manchuria was a factor that contributed to the surrender of Japan and the end of World War II” — but A15(5) refuses that sentence as the locator because it names a third event this atlas holds, `world-war-ii`, which here is the parent and not the cause; the lead sentence carries the edge.
